Documentation

Guides for every XRef workflow, generated from the Markdown in the repository. Start with the command reference on the home page, or the recorded Live Analysis walkthrough.

Command reference

xref refs

Find every instruction and data slot that names an address or a piece of text. It is the usual first step on a stripped binary: start from a string you can see in the program's output, find the code that uses it, then read that code with c or asm.

xref field

Recover the in-memory layout behind serialized keys. Give field the keys a program prints (JSON object keys, for example) and it finds the serializer code that emits them, the offset of each field relative to the serialized value, and, with --write, candidate code that writes those fields.

xref c

Decompile functions to structured, typed pseudo-C. c lifts the machine code of each function containing the given addresses: arguments, local variables, loops and branches, calls with their constant arguments, and string literals.

Linux live analysis: architecture and acceptance contract

Status: implemented across Stages L1 (PR #49), L2 (PR #53), L3 Increment 1 (PR #54), L3 Increment 2 (PR #55), and L4 for issue #46. Available starting with v0.3.0; the published v0.2.0 and earlier binaries do not contain xref live or the opt-in xref_live MCP tool.

Offline stacks and observed call evidence

symbolize maps addresses from a saved run onto the **selected executable**. It never attaches to a running process. Frames in another executable, a shared library, an ambiguous mapping, or a range without unwind information remain explicitly unresolved. These commands are available starting with v0.
